Borel-Moore homology (H∗BM​(X))

Words: 70
Homology (mathematics) OurBigBook.com
For a locally compact space, replace finite singular chains by chains for which every compact subset meets the images of only finitely many simplices with nonzero coefficients. The boundary operator preserves this local finiteness, giving the Borel-Moore chain complex and its homology. On a compact space it reduces to ordinary singular homology. A noncompact manifold has a locally finite fundamental class, with its orientation local system when necessary. The chain groups and homology are zero in negative degrees.

Generalized homology theory

Words: 43 Articles: 1
Homology (mathematics) OurBigBook.com
A generalized homology theory obeys the homotopy, exactness, suspension and wedge axioms, without imposing the ordinary dimension axiom. A represented homology theory is obtained by taking stable homotopy groups after a smash product of spectra.

Represented homology theory (E∗​(X))

Words: 20
Generalized homology theory OurBigBook.com
A topological spectrum E represents the reduced generalized homology theory Ek​(X)=πk​(E∧Σ∞X) on based spaces, where the smash product of spectra is derived. It is covariant in X.

Null-homologous cycle ([C]=0)

Words: 33
Homology (mathematics) OurBigBook.com
An element of a cycle module is null-homologous when it represents zero in homology, equivalently when it lies in the image of the boundary operator. A closed submanifold bounding a submanifold one dimension higher is null-homologous.

Primitive homology class (Δx=x⊗1+1⊗x)

Words: 30
Homology (mathematics) OurBigBook.com
A positive-degree class whose reduced homology diagonal vanishes. In a torsion-free homology Hopf algebra, powers of an even primitive class have binomial diagonals. Dualizing that diagonal produces the multiplication of a divided power algebra.

Acyclic space

Words: 29
Homology (mathematics) OurBigBook.com
A nonempty space is acyclic with the chosen coefficients if its reduced homology vanishes in every degree. Equivalently it has the homology of a point. It need not be contractible.

Homology of a directed union (Hi​(⋃a​Xa​)≅lim​a​Hi​(Xa​))

Words: 89 Articles: 1
Homology (mathematics) OurBigBook.com
Suppose X=⋃a​Xa​ is directed by inclusion and every compact subset of X lies in some Xa​. Every finite singular chain then lies in one Xa​, so C∗​(X)=lim​a​C∗​(Xa​). Exactness of filtered colimits gives
Hi​(X)≅lim​a​Hi​(Xa​).
(1)

Countability of the homology of an open Euclidean subset

Words: 57
Homology of a directed union OurBigBook.com
Every open subset U⊆RN is the directed union of finite unions of closed rational cubes contained in U. Every compact subset of U lies in one such finite polyhedron, whose homology is finitely generated. The homology of a directed union therefore expresses each Hi​(U;Z) as a direct limit over a countable family of countable groups, so it is countable.

Reduced homology (H∗​(X))

Words: 30
Homology (mathematics) OurBigBook.com
Reduced homology modifies degree zero so that a one-point space has zero homology in every degree. For a nonempty space, Hk​(X)=Hk​(X) when k>0, while H0​(X)≅H0​(X)⊕Z.

Homology group

Words: 60 Articles: 2
Homology (mathematics) OurBigBook.com
A homology group is one of the abelian groups produced by a homology theory. Its elements are homology classes, represented in singular homology by cycles modulo boundaries.

Zeroth homology group (H0​(X))

Words: 25
Homology group OurBigBook.com
The zeroth homology group is the free abelian group on the path components of X. In particular, if X has finitely many path components, then
H0​(X;Z)≅Z#π0​(X).
(2)

Homology class

Words: 12
Homology group OurBigBook.com
A homology class is an equivalence class of chain cycles modulo chain boundaries in a chain complex.

Functoriality of homology

Words: 74 Articles: 2
Homology (mathematics) OurBigBook.com
A continuous map f:X→Y induces homomorphisms f∗​:Hn​(X)→Hn​(Y) satisfying (g∘f)∗​=g∗​∘f∗​ and (idX​)∗​=idHn​(X)​.

Homotopy invariance of homology

Words: 60 Articles: 1
Functoriality of homology OurBigBook.com
Homotopic maps induce the same homomorphism on every homology group. Consequently, homotopy equivalent spaces have isomorphic homology groups.

Singular prism operator (∂P+P∂=g#​−f#​)

Words: 46
Homotopy invariance of homology OurBigBook.com
Triangulate Δq×I by the simplices with vertices (v0​,0),…,(vi​,0),(vi​,1),…,(vq​,1) and coefficients (−1)i. Composing with a homotopy between f and g gives a degree-one map P on singular chains. Shared faces cancel; the remaining faces give the displayed chain homotopy identity. Hence homotopic maps induce the same map on singular homology.

First homology (H1​(X))

Words: 23
Homology (mathematics) OurBigBook.com
The first homology group H1​(X) is the group of one-dimensional cycles modulo boundaries. For a path-connected space it is the abelianization of the fundamental group.

Singular homology

Words: 437 Articles: 9
Homology (mathematics) OurBigBook.com
Singular homology forms a chain complex from formal sums of continuous maps from standard simplices into a topological space. Its homology groups are invariant under homotopy.

Singular chain complex (C∗​(X;R))

Words: 32
Singular homology OurBigBook.com
The chain complex whose degree-n group is freely generated over R by the singular simplices σ:Δn→X. Its boundary is the alternating sum of restrictions to codimension-one faces. The homology of this complex is singular homology.

Small singular chains for an open cover (C∗U​(X)↪C∗​(X))

Words: 71
Singular homology OurBigBook.com
For an open cover, take the subcomplex generated by singular simplices whose images lie in single cover members. Repeated barycentric subdivision makes each finite singular chain small, and the standard subdivision chain homotopy shows that inclusion induces homology isomorphisms. For a two-set cover, the short exact sequence of these small chains gives the Mayer–Vietoris sequence; excising the complement of one open set from the pair with the other set gives its equivalent relative-homology formulation.

Local coefficient system

Words: 104 Articles: 1
Singular homology OurBigBook.com
A local coefficient system assigns an Abelian group or module to each point, with compatible transport isomorphisms along paths depending only on homotopy relative endpoints. Equivalently it is a functor from the fundamental groupoid. On a connected manifold it is described by a representation of the fundamental group after fixing one fiber.

Orientation local system (OM​)

Words: 54
Local coefficient system OurBigBook.com
Its fiber at x is Hn​(M,M∖{x};Z)≅Z. Transport changes its generator by the sign of local orientation along the path. For a connected nonorientable manifold, its degree-zero cohomology is zero, because no nonzero integer is invariant under sign reversal, whereas its degree-zero homology is Z/2, the coinvariants under that reversal.

Betti number (bk​=dimR​Hk​(M;R))

Words: 114 Articles: 1
Singular homology OurBigBook.com
A Betti number is the dimension of a real singular homology group; on a smooth manifold it is also the dimension of the corresponding de Rham cohomology group. For a finite-dimensional cohomology group on a closed Riemannian manifold, it equals the dimension of its space of harmonic representatives. Betti numbers can increase under a finite cover, so equality is a separate hypothesis, not a general covering-space theorem.

Poincaré polynomial (PM​(t)=∑i​bi​ti)

Words: 52
Betti number OurBigBook.com
For a space with finite-dimensional homology over a specified field and only finitely many nonzero Betti numbers, this polynomial records their graded dimensions. Its value at one is the total Betti number, and its value at minus one is the Euler characteristic. The Künneth theorem gives PM×N​(t)=PM​(t)PN​(t) over a field. For integer homology ranks, use the rational Betti numbers.

Singular chain (Cn​(X))

Words: 66 Articles: 1
Singular homology OurBigBook.com
A singular n-chain is a finite formal integer linear combination of singular simplices. Its support is contained in a compact subset of the ambient space.

Singular chain group (Cq​(X;Z))

Words: 41
Singular chain OurBigBook.com
The singular chain group is the free abelian group on all continuous maps Δq→X, the singular simplices. In particular it is free even when the set of simplices is infinite. This freeness makes applying Hom(Cq​(X),−) to a short exact coefficient sequence exact.

Singular simplex

Words: 27
Singular homology OurBigBook.com
A singular n-simplex in a space X is a continuous map σ:Δn→X from the standard n-simplex. Its alternating restrictions to the faces form its boundary.

Intersection form (QM​)

Words: 734 Articles: 12
Homology (mathematics) OurBigBook.com
For an oriented compact manifold of dimension 4k, the intersection form is the bilinear pairing on middle-dimensional homology obtained by representing classes by transverse cycles and counting their signed intersection points. On an oriented four-manifold it is equivalently the cup-product pairing on H2 evaluated on the fundamental class.
The intersection form of a 4-manifold is the four-dimensional case of this middle-dimensional intersection pairing.

Rank-one intersection form and the projective-plane cohomology ring (H∗(X;Z)≅Z[u]/(u3))

Words: 58
Intersection form OurBigBook.com
For a simply connected closed four-manifold with second Betti number one, Poincare duality and the universal coefficient theorem for cohomology make H2​ torsion-free of rank one. The integral intersection form is unimodular, so its one-by-one matrix is [1] or [−1]. Hence the square of a generator u∈H2 generates H4, giving the displayed cohomology ring. This is a ring isomorphism; it need not preserve a preassigned orientation class.

Positive index of the intersection form (b2+​(X))

Words: 35
Intersection form OurBigBook.com
For a closed oriented smooth four-manifold, b2+​ is the dimension of a maximal positive-definite subspace of its real intersection form. A symplectic form forces b2+​≥1, because its cohomology class has positive square. Reversing orientation exchanges the positive and negative indices.

Intersection form of a product of two closed oriented surfaces (QΣg​×Σh​​≅H⊕(1+2gh))

Words: 71
Intersection form OurBigBook.com
Here H is the hyperbolic form with matrix (01​10​). The degree-two cohomology consists of the two factor orientation classes and 4gh products of degree-one classes. The factor classes pair once and have zero squares. In symplectic bases ai​,bi​ and cj​,dj​, (ai​cj​)(bk​dl​)=−δik​δjl​ω1​ω2​ and (ai​dj​)(bk​cl​)=δik​δjl​ω1​ω2​. Each pair (i,j) contributes two hyperbolic forms; the fiber classes contribute one more. The sign in the first formula comes from interchanging two odd-degree factors.

Unimodular intersection pairing (L∼​Hom(L,Z))

Words: 52
Intersection form OurBigBook.com
An integral intersection form on a finite-rank free abelian group L is unimodular if its adjoint x↦λ(x,−) is an isomorphism to the integral dual. In an integral basis, this is equivalent to the pairing matrix having determinant 1 or −1, not merely nonzero determinant. For example, projective lines generate a unimodular intersection form on the Complex projective plane, with matrix (1) in its complex orientation.

Novikov additivity

Words: 50
Intersection form OurBigBook.com
When compact oriented four-manifolds are glued along an entire closed boundary three-manifold, the signature of the result is the sum of their intersection form signatures. It applies to X0​∪∂X0​​(−X1​) with the difference of the two signatures. Gluing along only part of a boundary can require a correction; that is a different situation.

Intersection pairing (Hk​(W)×Hn−k​(W,∂W)→F)

Words: 227 Articles: 3
Intersection form OurBigBook.com
An intersection pairing counts signed intersections of transverse representatives of complementary homology classes, using one relative representative when the manifold has boundary. With F2​ coefficients it is defined without orientation choices. Poincare-Lefschetz duality makes this a perfect pairing for compact manifolds.

Intersection matrix (Mij​=Di​⋅Dj​)

Words: 30
Intersection pairing OurBigBook.com
The intersection matrix records an intersection pairing on chosen classes. Its nonsingularity proves linear independence: a relation between the classes, paired with each class in turn, gives a vector in the matrix's kernel.

Coordinate sphere intersection basis ([SI​]⋅[SJ​]=1 if J=Ic,0 otherwise)

Words: 92
Intersection pairing OurBigBook.com
In the product (S2d)2ℓ, for d,ℓ≥1, vary the factors indexed by an ℓ-element subset I and fix points in the other factors. Orient the resulting submanifold SI​ in increasing factor order. These homology classes form an integral middle-dimensional basis by the Künneth theorem. Complementary subsets give a transverse intersection at one point, with positive sign since all factor dimensions are even. For noncomplementary subsets some factor is fixed in both representatives; moving that point makes them disjoint. In particular every basis class has zero self-intersection number. Complementary pairs give hyperbolic blocks in the intersection form.

Half-lives-half-dies theorem (dimkeri∗​=21​dimH1​(∂W;F2​))

Words: 70
Intersection pairing OurBigBook.com
For a compact three-manifold W, let L=ker(H1​(∂W;F2​)→H1​(W;F2​)). The boundary intersection pairing satisfies L⊥=L: the long exact sequence in relative homology identifies L with boundaries of relative surfaces, and the boundary-interior adjoint identity identifies its orthogonal complement with the same kernel. Hence 2dimL=dimH1​(∂W;F2​). This also implies that a closed surface with odd first mod-two Betti number, such as RP2, cannot be the entire boundary of a compact three-manifold.

Degree constraint from intersection forms (PTQM​P=(degf)QN​)

Words: 80
Intersection form OurBigBook.com
For a map f:M→N of connected closed oriented four-manifolds, naturality of the cup product gives
QM​(f∗u,f∗v)=(degf)QN​(u,v).
(3)
When degf=0, nondegeneracy makes f∗:H2(N;Q)→H2(M;Q) injective. Consequently the target intersection form, multiplied by the mapping degree, must embed into the source form. For equal second Betti numbers, a matrix P for pullback satisfies PTQM​P=(degf)QN​; taking determinants often rules out nonzero degrees. In particular, a two-dimensional indefinite source form cannot realize a nonzero multiple of a two-dimensional definite target form.

Real de Rham intersection form in dimension four (Q:HdR2​(N;R)2→R)

Words: 102 Articles: 1
Intersection form OurBigBook.com
On a compact oriented smooth manifold N of dimension four without boundary, set Q([α],[β])=∫N​α∧β for closed real two-forms. The Stokes theorem makes the expression independent of representatives, and the even degrees make it symmetric. It is the real de Rham cohomology version of the intersection form. The Hodge decomposition theorem and Hodge star operator express it as Q(h,k)=(h,∗k)L2​ on harmonic representatives.

Signature of the intersection form from harmonic duality (signatureQ=(b+,b−))

Words: 55
Real de Rham intersection form in dimension four OurBigBook.com
On a closed oriented Riemannian manifold of dimension four, the Hodge star operator preserves harmonic two-forms and splits them into orthogonal spaces H+ and H− with eigenvalues +1 and −1. The real de Rham intersection form in dimension four equals the positive L2 inner product on H+ and its negative on H−. It is nondegenerate, since Q(h,∗h)=∥h∥22​. Its signature pair is (dimH+,dimH−).

Homology of an equatorial sphere complement (Sn∖Sm≃Sn−m−1)

Words: 70
Homology of a sphere OurBigBook.com
For the standard coordinate inclusion of spheres, write points as (u,v)∈Rm+1×Rn−m, with v=0 in the complement. The map (u,v)↦(u,v/∥v∥) is a homeomorphism to Bopenm+1​×Sn−m−1, with inverse (u,w)↦(u,1−∥u∥2​w). Contracting the ball factor proves the displayed homotopy equivalence. In codimension one there are two contractible components, so integral H0​ is Z2; in higher codimension the only nonzero homology groups are H0​=Z and Hn−m−1​=Z.

Degree of a continuous mapping (degf)

Words: 2k Articles: 33
Homology (mathematics) OurBigBook.com
For a map f:Sm→Sm, the degree is the integer by which f∗​ multiplies a chosen generator of Hm​(Sm;Z). It is invariant under homotopy.

Mod-two degree of a map between closed manifolds (deg2​(f)∈F2​)

Words: 69
Degree of a continuous mapping OurBigBook.com
For a map f:M→N between closed connected n-manifolds, the mod-two degree is defined by f∗​[M]2​=deg2​(f)[N]2​. Every manifold has a mod-two orientation class, so no orientability assumption is needed. It is invariant under homotopy. A nonsurjective map has mod-two degree zero: mapping the fundamental classes into the local relative homology at a missed target point makes the source contribution zero but leaves the target local generator nonzero.

Nonzero degree from a sphere obstructs manifold products (degf=0⟹M≅Xk×Ym−k)

Words: 77
Degree of a continuous mapping OurBigBook.com
Suppose a map Sm→M of closed connected oriented manifolds has nonzero mapping degree. A product decomposition with 0<k<m would have oriented closed factors: an orientation-reversing loop in either factor, with the other coordinate fixed, would reverse the product orientation. Pull back their top orientation classes to obtain α∈Hk(M;Z) and β∈Hm−k(M;Z) with α⌣β a generator of Hm(M;Z). Both pullbacks to the sphere vanish in their intermediate degrees, contradicting the nonzero-degree pullback of their product.

Degrees of maps of the zero-sphere (degf∈{−1,0,1})

Words: 47
Degree of a continuous mapping OurBigBook.com
Define mapping degree for S0 using its rank-one reduced homology group H0​(S0;Z). Its generator is the difference of its two points. The four maps of that two-point set consist of the identity, the interchange, and two constant maps; their degree multipliers are 1,−1,0,0. Thus sphere maps of arbitrary integer degree require positive sphere dimension.

Relative mapping degree (F∗​[Dm,Sm−1]=d[Dm,Sm−1])

Words: 137 Articles: 2
Degree of a continuous mapping OurBigBook.com
For a map of oriented disk pairs, the multiplier on top relative homology is its relative mapping degree. Naturality of the connecting homomorphism identifies it with the mapping degree of the boundary map.

Graph intersection formula for mapping degree (deg(F∣∂Dm​)=(Dm×{0})⋅ΓF​)

Words: 70
Relative mapping degree OurBigBook.com
For a smooth map of disk pairs whose graph of a function is transverse to the zero slice, orient the graph by its domain. Let f be a chain map between degreewise finitely generated free abelian groups. If its reduction modulo every prime number is a quasi-isomorphism, the mapping cone acyclicity criterion makes M(f)⊗Fp​ acyclic. The short exact sequence of chain complexes 0→Mp​M→M⊗Fp​→0 implies that multiplication by p is an isomorphism on every Hi​(M). These are finitely generated abelian groups. Their free summands would make multiplication by p fail to be surjective, and any nonzero finite summand would make it fail to be injective for a prime dividing its order. Thus Hi​(M)=0 and f is a quasi-isomorphism. Degreewise finite generation is essential to this argument.

A relative cycle is represented by a singular chain b whose boundary lies in A. Define δ[bˉ]=[∂b]. If a representative changes by ∂c+a with a∈Cn​(A), its boundary changes by ∂a, an A-boundary. Thus the map is well-defined and additive. Its image is exactly the kernel of Hn−1​(A)→Hn−1​(B): a cycle in A dies in B precisely when it is the boundary of a relative cycle lifted to B. Poincare duality gives the displayed formula for connected closed oriented four-manifolds. Every integer occurs. A connected sum of r copies of the Complex projective plane and s copies of S1×S3 has Euler characteristic 2+r−2s, because the summand characteristics are three and zero. Given any integer h, choose s large enough that r=h−2+2s≥0; when both counts are zero use S4. If simple connectivity is additionally required, the possible values instead begin at two, since b1​=0; connected sums of projective planes realize every such value.

Ordinary vertex in a nonconcurrent great-circle arrangement

Words: 110
Euler characteristic OurBigBook.com
A finite set of distinct great circles not all passing through a common antipodal pair has a vertex lying on exactly two circles. Its cells are spherical polygons with at least three edges: a digon would have antipodal endpoints, and every circle's defining hemisphere would then have to contain both endpoints, forcing a common axis. With V−E+F=2 and 3F≤2E, the graph has a vertex of valence less than six. Valences are even and at least four, so one is exactly four. Central projection identifies this with an ordinary intersection in a real projective line arrangement. If affine line intersections are counted only at finite points, parallel-line configurations require a separate qualification.
